traceability.notes: Performance data extracted by claude-sonnet-5 reading the PDF directly (native document input), used as a fallback because the deterministic pdfplumber pipeline (summary_report_parser.py) found no per-category breakdown in this report. Model's own extraction notes: The report presents four raw-data tables (Spreading 45h, Spreading 72h, Spiral 45h, Spiral 72h) in Appendix 5, each with the same two food categories (labelled '1' = meat products and '2' = dairy products based on product examples: pork chop, chicken, etc. for category 1; mozzarella, milk, cheese, cream for category 2). I selected the 'Spreading method 72h' table as the primary/canonical result since the spreading method at 72h is the standard reading time referenced in the main body conclusions (results available at day 2 = 48h-72h) and is listed first among the reference-method comparisons in the accuracy profile section. The other three variants (Spreading 45h: cat1 bias -0.21/SD 0.22/n19, cat2 bias 0.01/SD 0.39/n19; Spiral 45h: cat1 bias -0.09/SD 0.30/n15, cat2 bias 0.20/SD 0.59/n16; Spiral 72h: cat1 bias not given (blank/0 in source, likely incomplete calculation), cat2 bias 0.22/SD 0.56/n17) are alternative reading times/methods and were not included as separate categories per instructions. Category names 'a/b/c' subtypes within each category (e.g., meat: a=beef/lamb, b=poultry, c=cured/processed meats; dairy: a=pasteurized, b=raw milk, c=desserts) were not broken out as they appear to be sample-type subdivisions within the two main ISO 16140-2 categories (meat products, dairy products), not distinct top-level categories. The Acceptability Limit (0.5 log) was taken from the accuracy profile tables (Table 15/16), which is consistent across the whole report. 'All categories' summary rows were excluded per instructions.
